text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG said on Thursday that 1996 sales rose 11 percent to 15.96 billion Swiss francs ($11.6 billion) and profits were again expected to rise.
Roche, the second largest Swiss pharmaceuticals firm, said a significant gain in volume sales helped it boost its position in key markets and sectors, despite downward pressure on prices.

Sales of Roche's leading products, such as Rocephin -- the world's top-selling injectable antibiotic -- continued to grow and new products, such as the AIDS drug Invirase, were very well received by the market.
Roche said its operating results had strengthened on the back of higher capacity utilisation in its factories and steady gains in efficiency.
"Taking into account another good result for the group's non-operating activities as well, Roche expects to see consolidated net income increase once again," Roche said in a statement.
Roche's profit forecast is similar to its previous forecast from October, when it also forecast that 1996 profits would exceed 1995's group net profit of 3.37 billion Swiss francs.
Measured in local currencies, Roche's 1996 sales were up eight percent.
Roche's pharmaceuticals division, the largest division, showed a sales gain of 13 percent to 10.5 billion francs. In local currencies sales were up 10 percent.

Higher drugs sales were achieved not only in North America and Europe -- the two most important markets -- but also in Brazil, Mexico, Australia and other major markets. Solid volume growth in Japan helped offset a decline in revenue from the government's mandated price cuts.
Sales at Roche's second largest division, Vitamins and fine chemicals, rose nine percent to 3.3 billion francs, despite intense competition.
Sales growth was especially strong for water-soluble vitamins and sales increases were achieved in North and Latin America, while sales in the Far East were below expectations.
Roche also increased its market share significantly in the diagnostics business, a market characterised by stagnant demand and pressure on prices.
Sales from the diagnostics division rose 18 percent last year to 755 million francs.
However, sales from Roche's Fragrances and Flavours division fell two percent to 1.4 billion francs as general economic conditions put a damper on the entire industry.
Sales of fragrances were up by a healthy margin in the Americas and Asia, but the European market suffered from continuing weak demand for luxury perfumes, Roche said.
